restated_task: Implement brackets.is_balanced(s) in the existing stub so that string inputs return a bool indicating whether the ASCII brackets (), [] and {} are correctly matched and nested. Ignore all other characters, accept empty strings and strings containing no brackets as balanced, and raise TypeError for every non-string input. Preserve is_bracket, existing package imports, and all existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept str instances, including subclasses. Ignore every character other than (, ), [, ], { and }. Return True exactly when every closing bracket matches the most recent unmatched opening bracket and no opening brackets remain unmatched at the end; otherwise return False. Return an actual bool. Empty strings and strings without bracket characters return True. Remain available through from brackets import is_balanced.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str, including bytes, None, numbers, booleans, lists and other containers; do not coerce inputs to strings.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation and public import. Return True exactly when c is a str instance of length one containing one of the six ASCII bracket characters; return False otherwise.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket both succeed.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}' and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
4. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}' and '())'.
5. Each standalone opening or closing bracket returns False; premature closing brackets, such as in ')(', and leftover opening brackets, such as in '(()', return False.
6. Repeated nesting and successive balanced groups are accepted, including '((()))' and '[{}]([])'.

7. All non-bracket characters are ignored, including whitespace, newlines, Unicode characters, quotes and backslashes. Strings containing no ASCII brackets return True. Quotes and backslashes do not escape brackets or suppress matching.
8. Removing every non-bracket character from any string leaves its is_balanced result unchanged.
9. Every successful call returns an object whose type is bool, for both balanced and unbalanced string inputs.
10. Non-string inputs raise TypeError, including None, True, 0, 1.5, b'()', [], (), {}, and an arbitrary object instance. Empty containers are not treated as balanced.
11. Instances of str subclasses are accepted and evaluated using the same bracket rules as ordinary strings.
12. is_bracket remains unchanged: it returns True for each character in '()[]{}' and False for 'a', '', '((', and 1. Existing tests remain unchanged and pass.
out_of_scope: Changing is_bracket or any existing tests.
Changing the public function signatures or package exports.
Adding support for other bracket types, language syntax, quoting or escape rules.
